pairs.difference: A is the real lighthouse from the lessons: a red tower with neutral white-grey stone that goes blue-grey in shadow, and a calm blue sky. In B the house walls are a warm mauve-brown that reads as one muddy mass in the lens. The purple roof, saturated lime-green hill and yellow windows are all loud at once, giving 5 hue families with no neutral resting area.
pairs.fix: Paint the house walls in a cool neutral grey stone with blue-grey shadows. Make the roof a muted dusty purple and the grass a softer, less acid green, so the yellow windows are the only bright accent.

pairs.difference: A: the seahorse is orange with a yellow belly against a graded blue sea, a clean warm-on-cool hero. B: the four balloons are each a pure, fully saturated hue (red, orange, teal, purple), giving 5.45 hue families, above the real range. There is no muted or neutral color on the hero; only the clouds rest the eye.
pairs.fix: Use two or three balloon colors with natural rubber shading, darker and slightly less saturated on the shadow side. Drop one hue family.

pairs.difference: A: the red gloves sit on an orange wood table in front of a blue wall, and the glove shadows stay a rich deep red. B: the cauldron is near-black and the floor is a desaturated purple-grey. The only chroma is the acid green brew and a small pink wall strip, so subject chroma (0.038) and shadow chroma (0.385) are below every real card. The color looks drained, not chosen.
pairs.fix: Give the cauldron a dark iron color with a cool blue-purple sheen. Make the floor stones a richer slate blue-violet, and let the green brew cast a soft green tint on the rim.

pairs.difference: A: the yellow duck has a red seat and beak, a blue base, green rays behind and yellow sand, a clear hero against its background. B: an orange pumpkin sits on orange wood, with orange-pink shadows on the table. The hero and the floor share one hue family, the warm share is 0.648, and only the purple wall separates them.
pairs.fix: Make the wooden table a cooler, greyer brown, and put a deep purple-blue shadow under the pumpkin, so the orange pumpkin is the only strong orange on the card.

pairs.difference: A: a beige stone fountain with cyan water on a yellow striped wall and orange-beige tiles; the cool water breaks up the warm card. B: a black cat with a red collar on a yellow wall and orange wood floor. The card is 100% warm with 1.46 hue families, below the real range. The cat is a flat black-brown with no cool reflection, and its shadows on the floor are orange.
pairs.fix: Add cool blue-grey sheen to the cat's black fur on the top edges, and make the floor shadow a cooler brown-violet. Optionally make the wall a softer, less orange yellow.

pairs.difference: A: blue sneakers with green and teal trim on an orange and cream background, a strong cool hero against a warm field. B: a grey tombstone on a yellow-orange glow background. The stone takes on the warm cast, and its shadows go to a khaki grey instead of a cool grey. Subject chroma is 0.018, far below real cards, and the warm share is 0.969.
pairs.fix: Paint the tombstone a cool blue-grey stone with blue-violet shadows, and keep the green moss and orange flower as small accents against the warm background.

pairs.difference: A: a black witch hat with a purple band on concentric orange rings. The hat's shadows are a flat dull purple-black (shadow chroma 0.484, below every real card), and the card is 86% warm. B: a navy graduation cap with an orange-gold tassel on cyan rings. Its shadows stay a rich related blue, and the gold trim is the only accent.
pairs.fix: Paint the hat a deep blue-violet black, with saturated purple in the shadow folds and a cool highlight on the brim. Make the orange background rings less dominant.

pairs.difference: A: a gold candelabra on purple rays, a clean complementary split between hero and background. B: a brass oil lamp on yellow-green rays. The lamp's gold, the glass and the glow all sit in the same yellow-green family as the background, so in the lens the hero merges with the rays.
pairs.fix: Put the lamp on a cooler, deeper teal or blue-green background, and keep the glass chimney a pale neutral, so the warm brass reads as the hero.

pairs.difference: A: a lavender-grey stone chess table on green grass. The stone stays neutral and its shadows go cool, much like the real lion statue. B: an orange-brown coffin with purple lining on saturated green grass under a yellow moon. The wood reads as a pushed orange, its shadow side goes to a hot dark brown, and the grass is as loud as the hero.
pairs.fix: Paint the coffin a darker, desaturated walnut brown with cool shadows. Calm the grass to a softer green, and keep the purple lining as the single accent.

pairs.difference: A: an orange drink with a red straw and a cyan umbrella on a purple diamond background, a loud but clearly role-split palette like the real cards. B: a pale blue crystal ball on a gold stand, set on orange wood against a green diamond wall. The gold stand and the warm wood sit in one warm block, and the cool glass is pale and washed out against the saturated green.
pairs.fix: Give the crystal ball a deeper blue-violet core with a bright highlight. Make the wooden table a cooler, greyer brown so the gold stand stands out.

pairs.difference: A: an orange broom with yellow straw on a blue wave background, only 1.52 hue families, below the real range. The broom is a small single-warm-hue mass and its straw shadows stay the same orange. B: a red scarf with a gold badge on cyan swirls. It is very saturated (subject chroma 0.2165), but the red shadows stay rich and related, as on the real red cards.
pairs.fix: Give the broom a darker brown handle with a cooler shadow side and paler, straw-colored bristles with brown-olive shadow, plus a small accent color on the binding.

pairs.difference: A: orange flip-flops with yellow straps on a teal striped background, two clear hue roles like the real cards. B: blue, magenta and green books on a lavender-grey shelf with a blue window. The lens shows 9.58 hue families, about twice the real maximum. The room is a muddy purple-grey (background chroma 0.071), and the book shadows go teal and purple, unrelated to each local color.
pairs.fix: Use two book colors with shadows that are a darker version of each cover. Make the room a single clean, saturated color behind them, and drop the extra window blue and the brown drawer.

pattern: Generated cards give themselves away in two ways. Either the whole card is pulled into one warm family (hero, floor and shadows all orange or yellow, as with the pumpkin, black cat, tombstone and witch hat), or the hero's darks lose chroma and go flat black or khaki instead of a rich, related shadow hue. The second failure is hue overload, where every part is a different pure hue with no neutral to rest the eye. Real cards keep neutrals cool (white and grey go blue-grey in shadow), split hero and background into clear complementary roles, and keep shadows as a deeper version of the local color.
